newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr and debt market recover strength at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr and debt market recover strength at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.07 (PREV 91.99) 90-DAYS 8.30 (PREV 8.38)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.10 PCT (PREV 8.10) US 5-YR 6.07 (PREV 5.91)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 746.83 (PREV 741.87) Reuters NZ MCI -78 vs -83
New Zealand bank bill yields came down from their highs by the close on Monday as they responded to a firming in the kiwi dollar.
Dealers said the kiwi ended bid as the interbank market attempted to square its short position.

The debt market opened very weak in response to a big selloff in the U.S. on Friday on robust jobs data and as the Monetary Conditions Index eased to 40 basis points beyond the Reserve Bank's comfort zone.
However, as the currency regained some strength and the MCI lifted to 746, the bills strengthened. The 90-days ended at 8.30 percent from 8.42 percent mid-morning.
Direction for the currency and the debt market is seen as heavily dependent on jobs data due on Tuesday.

If the data is in line with the Reserve Bank's forecasts, the debt market will sell off and the currency will rise, while a number in line with the weaker forecasts of the private sector will have the market looking for the RB to sanction the easing of recent days.
Dealers said the market was thin and lacklustre with Australia on holiday.
"The market is looking for a soft number and either an easing or at least a widening of the (RBNZ's tolerance on) MCI," an Auckland dealer said.
"If the data was weak enough then I think certain people are expecting a statement from the bank," he said, adding that he personally did not expect a formal statement from the bank.
"The market will do it," he said.
Economists forecast the unemployment rate will rise to 6.9 percent from 6.4 percent and jobs growth in the June quarter will be negative 0.15 percent from positive 1.1 percent in the March quarter.
A number to be watched will be the rise or fall in the hours worked. The Reserve Bank has forecast a 1.9 percent rise in the June quarter against private sector forecasts of 1.0-1.5 percent.
The bank said this figure is a good indicator because employers can relatively easily adjust the numbers of hours worked according to economic conditions.
A bond dealer said the market was becoming comfortable with the MCI at 80 to 90 points easier than the RB's desired level and was likely to push to 100 to test the RB's resolve.
He said the debt market response to the jobs number will depend on the currency reaction which could be erratic.
